title.value: A Complete Characterization of One-More Assumptions in the Algebraic Group Model
A Complete Characterization of One-More Assumptions in the Algebraic Group Model

abstract.value: One-more problems like One-More Discrete Logarithm (OMDL) and One-More Diffie-Hellman (OMDH) have found wide use in cryptography, due to their ability to naturally model security definitions for interactive primitives like blind signatures and oblivious pseudorandom functions (OPRF). Furthermore, a generalization of OMDH called Threshold OMDH (TOMDH) has proven useful for building threshold versions of interactive protocols. However, due to their complexity it is often unclear how hard such problems actually are, leading cryptographers to analyze them in idealized models like the Generic Group Mo del (GGM) and Algebraic Group Model (AGM). In this work we give a complete characterization of widely used group-based one-more problems in the AGM, using the Q-DL hierarchy of assumptions defined in the work of Bauer, Fuchsbauer and Loss [BFL20]. 1. Regarding (T)OMDH, we show (T)OMDH is part of the Q-DL hierarchy in the AGM; in particular, Q-OMDH is equivalent to Q-DL. Along the way w e find and repair a flaw in the original GGM hardness proof of TOMDH [JKKX17, Theorem 7], thereby giving the first correct proof that TOMDH is hard in the GGM. 2. Regarding OMDL, we show the Q-OMDL problems constitute an infinite hierarchy of problems in the AGM incomparable to the Q-DL hierarchy; that is, Q-OMDL is strictly harder than Q-OMDL if Q < Q , and Q-OMDL is incomparable to Q-DL (i.e., there are no reductions either way) unless Q = Q = 0. We give two practical applications of the above results. 1. We give formal evidence for a folklore conjecture that the best known attack on the widely used OPAQUE asymmetric PAKE protocol is due to Cheon [Che06]. 2. We show that threshold schemes reliant on TOMDH have the same level of concrete security as non-threshold v ersions, thus achieving threshold security "for free".
